Name: Sundance Film Festival
City: Park City and Salt Lake City, Utah
Founded: 1978 (as the Utah/US Film Festival, Salt Lake City; renamed the Sundance Film Festival in 1991)
2027 Dates: 21–31 January 2027, in Boulder, Colorado — the festival's new home (officially announced by the Sundance Institute)
Leadership: Eugene Hernandez, Director, Sundance Film Festival and Public Programming; Amanda Kelso, Acting CEO, Sundance Institute; Kim Yutani, Director of Programming
Principal Venues: Theatres across Park City and Salt Lake City for the final Utah edition. Announced Boulder venues from 2027 include the Boulder Theater, Chautauqua Auditorium, Macky Auditorium and the Roe Green Theatre (University of Colorado Boulder) and Cinemark Century Boulder
Sections: U.S. Dramatic Competition; U.S. Documentary Competition; World Cinema Dramatic Competition; World Cinema Documentary Competition; NEXT; Premieres; Midnight; Shorts
Top Awards: Grand Jury Prizes (U.S. and World Cinema, dramatic and documentary); Audience Awards; Festival Favorite Award
Scale (as published): 16,201 submissions in total for 2026, including 4,255 feature films; 90 feature films selected, 40% of them by first-time filmmakers (Sundance Institute figures, December 2025)
Industry Market: No attached sales market; Sundance is the year's first major acquisitions arena, with distribution deals negotiated on site during the festival
Contact: Festival information and submissions via festival.sundance.org; Sundance Institute at sundance.org
Notes: Founded in Salt Lake City in August 1978 by Robert Redford and partners as the Utah/US Film Festival; moved to Park City in 1981 and took the Sundance name in 1991. The 2026 edition closed more than four decades in Utah; the festival's biggest on-site deal that year was A24's acquisition of US rights to The Invite, reported at more than US$10 million. Founder Robert Redford, who died in September 2025, had given his blessing to the Boulder move before his death.
Sources: Sundance Institute programme announcement, December 2025 (via Filmmaker Magazine); Screen Daily (2026 edition report; 2027 Boulder dates and venues); Associated Press (2027 dates and venues); sundance.org (2027 festival); festival histories (1978 founding)
